title: Offline-First Notes App
prompt: Design a notes frontend that opens and edits existing notes offline, survives refresh and synchronizes on reconnect. A sync API supports versions and tombstones. Explain local durability, concurrent edits, quota failures and service worker updates. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Read and edit locally without waiting for network
Atomically persist note edits and a pending mutation outbox
Sync with version conflicts and explicit deletion tombstones
nonFunctionalReqs: 1,000 notes averaging 10 KB text; offline app shell; browser storage can be evicted and is not a backup guarantee.
Keyboard-accessible note list/editor, labelled sync and conflict status, explicit unsaved errors and focus preservation when remote notes arrive.
On 409 keep both versions for merge; never silently overwrite. On transaction failure retain in-memory draft, show unsaved and allow export. A network online flag alone does not prove sync succeeded.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: Write Note and OutboxMutation atomically to IndexedDB before acknowledging saved locally. A foreground sync coordinator retries stable mutation IDs, uses expectedVersion and stores remote tombstones. Service worker caches the versioned app shell, not arbitrary private API responses; background sync is optional enhancement.
Local and remote versions diverge, or storage write fails
Online-first is simpler when offline edits are unnecessary. CRDTs help concurrent rich editing but add substantial complexity for basic notes.
